now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3#17
now.text: Yo-Yo and Lincoln Campbell fight side by side in Daisy's Secret Warriors, including the mission where they bring in Gideon Malick. When Coulson suspects one of them is under Hive's control, they both stand up to him.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Secret Warriors teammate who fights beside Yo-Yo and stands up to Coulson.
now.on_b_card_about_a: Secret Warriors teammate who fights beside Lincoln and stands up to Coulson.

proposed.text: Yo-Yo and Lincoln Campbell fight side by side in Daisy's Secret Warriors and bring in Gideon Malick, and they stand up to Coulson when he suspects one of them is under Hive's control. When the Kree device turns up in Lincoln's locker, Yo-Yo tries to take him down, and his electricity knocks her out.

changes.evidence: The Team (S3 ep 17): when Coulson finds the Kree beacon in Lincoln's locker, Yo-Yo goes at Lincoln with Overpowering Tape. His electricity knocks her out, he is locked up, and she leaves S.H.I.E.L.D. The current text stops before this and leaves them as teammates.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4#21
now.text: Piper is one of the agents who pull Fitz out of the chamber where he has trapped Aida.
now.on_a_card_about_b: An agent who helps pull Fitz out of Aida's chamber.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A scientist Piper helps pull from the chamber where he traps Aida.

proposed.text: When Aida turns on Fitz in the containment chamber they are locked in together, Piper is one of the agents who pull him out, and she gets him away to the Zephyr.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A scientist Piper pulls out of Aida's chamber and gets to the Zephyr.

changes.evidence: The Return (S4 ep 21): the team locks Fitz and Aida in a Containment Chamber together. When Fitz rejects her, Aida attacks him, and Piper, Davis and Prince pull Fitz out. Fitz never traps Aida, so 'the chamber where he has trapped Aida' (text and Piper's card) is wrong.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5#17
now.text: Ruby Hale is raised to see Quake as the rival she must beat to earn her mother's approval. She hunts Daisy down and attacks her with her chakram blade.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Hale's daughter, raised to beat Quake. Hunts Daisy down and attacks her with a chakram.
now.on_b_card_about_a: The rival Ruby is raised to beat to earn Hale's approval.

proposed.text: Ruby Hale is raised to see Quake as the rival she must beat to earn her mother's approval. When Daisy saves Coulson and Talbot from her, Ruby tells Daisy she wants to beat her and attacks with her chakram, but Daisy knocks her out.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Hale's daughter, raised to beat Quake. Attacks Daisy with a chakram and loses.

changes.evidence: The Honeymoon (S5 ep 17): Ruby is chasing Coulson and Talbot, not Daisy. Daisy steps in, they fight, and Daisy's shockwave knocks Ruby out. 'Hunts Daisy down' does not match the episode.

now.title: Ant-Man
now.text: Maggie is Cassie's mother. She raises Cassie with Jim Paxton and urges Scott to keep his promise to stay out of crime for their daughter's sake.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Cassie's mother, who raises her with Jim Paxton.
now.on_b_card_about_a: Maggie's daughter. Maggie urges Scott to stay out of crime for their daughter's sake.

proposed.text: Maggie is Cassie's mother. She raises Cassie with her fiance Jim Paxton and tells Scott that if he wants to see their daughter, he must get a job and a place and pay child support, and be the hero Cassie already thinks he is.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Maggie's daughter. Maggie tells Scott to be the hero Cassie thinks he is.

changes.evidence: Ant-Man: at Cassie's party Maggie tells Scott to find an apartment, get a job and pay child support, and to 'be the person she already thinks you are'. The promise to give up crime comes only from the tie-in comic (Ant-Man: Scott Lang: Small Time), not the film.

owner_calls.question: Stage 0 (S7#12) is 'enemy', but by the end of the episode Nathaniel has left Garrett to die, Garrett agrees to help, and he teleports Yo-Yo, May and Coulson out of the Lighthouse (Yo-Yo and May had refused to unlock him) before Victoria Hand shoots him. Keep 'enemy', or change it to 'ally' and add the turn to the text?
options: Keep enemy (he only helps under duress and dies minutes later)
Change to ally and add: 'Betrayed by Nathaniel, Garrett agrees to teleport Yo-Yo, May and Coulson out, and is shot dead on arrival.'
owner_calls.evidence: The End Is at Hand (S7 ep 12)

owner_calls.question: Stage 2 (S5#20) and other Talbot stages in this chunk (with Daisy, Hale and Robin) call him 'Graviton'. Fandom cites only a Marvel.com interview for that codename, and I could not confirm that it is said on screen. Keep 'Graviton', or use plain wording such as 'after absorbing the Gravitonium'?
owner_calls.evidence: Talbot's codename field on Fandom is sourced to a Marvel.com interview, not an episode
